sentences.en: I couldn't figure it out.
sentences.zh: 我当时没搞明白。

sentences.en: I was hitting on a lot of straight people.
sentences.zh: 我当时在向很多异性恋者示好。

sentences.en: This is Anna Pulley.
sentences.zh: 这是安娜·普利。

sentences.en: She's a writer.
sentences.zh: 她是一位作家。

sentences.en: And when she moved from Chicago to San Francisco, she didn't know who to hit on anymore.
sentences.zh: 当她从芝加哥搬到旧金山时，她不知道该向谁示好了。

sentences.en: Midwestern queer culture is extremely different than Bay Area queer culture.
sentences.zh: 中西部的酷儿文化与湾区的酷儿文化截然不同。

sentences.en: And one of the things that was most noticeable to me was fashion.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，最明显的一点就是时尚。

sentences.en: Some of the queer signals from the Midwest didn't quite hold, like plaid flannel shirts.
sentences.zh: 中西部的一些酷儿信号在这里不太管用，比如格子法兰绒衬衫。

sentences.en: I wear flannel and I feel gayer.
sentences.zh: 我穿上法兰绒，感觉自己更像个酷儿了。

sentences.en: In the Midwest, way more so, I think.
sentences.zh: 我想在中西部，这种感觉要强烈得多。

sentences.en: If you are part of a group, there are things you can wear or ways you can style your hair, signs that show that you are part of that group.
sentences.zh: 如果你属于某个群体，你可以通过穿着或发型来展示一些标志，表明你是该群体的一员。

sentences.en: Flannel was one way to signify, like, I exiSt.
sentences.zh: 法兰绒就是一种表达方式，就像在说，我存在。

sentences.en: But you can't really stop other people from wearing these signals.
sentences.zh: 但你无法阻止其他人穿戴这些标志。

sentences.en: And so eventually the power of that signal gets diluted.
sentences.zh: 所以最终，这种信号的力量被稀释了。

sentences.en: So if you see someone wearing plaid now, does it mean anything to you?
sentences.zh: 那么如果你现在看到有人穿格子衫，这对你来说意味着什么吗？

sentences.en: Well, I might first think, are you a bike messenger?
sentences.zh: 嗯，我首先可能会想，你是骑行快递员吗？

sentences.en: And then the next thing you know, you can't even tell what clothing is signaling what anymore.
sentences.zh: 然后你会发现，你甚至分不清什么衣服代表什么信号了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: One night I was rebuffed by this straight lady and I got upset about it.
sentences.zh: 有一天晚上，我被一位异性恋女士拒绝了，我为此感到难过。

sentences.en: And also I'd been thinking about hipsters a lot because they appropriate a lot of working class culture motifs.
sentences.zh: 而且我一直在思考嬉皮士，因为他们挪用了许多工人阶级的文化元素。

sentences.en: And flannel is one of them.
sentences.zh: 法兰绒就是其中之一。

sentences.en: So it doesn't seem like lesbians are appropriating working class wear?
sentences.zh: 所以，这看起来不像是女同性恋者在挪用工人阶级的服装吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: So that's interesting.
sentences.zh: 这很有趣。

sentences.en: I don't know who actually owns, you know, if anyone can own a fabric.
sentences.zh: 我不知道谁真正拥有这些，你知道，如果有人能拥有一种面料的话。

sentences.en: Articles of intereSt.
sentences.zh: 有趣的物件。

sentences.en: A show about what we wear.
sentences.zh: 一个关于我们穿什么的节目。

sentences.en: And so maybe the ideas about clothing.
sentences.zh: 也许还有关于服装的理念。

sentences.en: You can attach.
sentences.zh: 你可以附加的。

sentences.en: Our ideas about class.
sentences.zh: 我们关于阶级的观念。

sentences.en: An idea of home to a piece of cloth.
sentences.zh: 一种将家的概念赋予一块布料。

sentences.en: These are best for laSt.
sentences.zh: 这些最耐穿。

sentences.en: Any fool can wear clothes.
sentences.zh: 任何傻瓜都能穿衣服。

sentences.en: But if you ain't got the attitude and style to carry it off, man, you're just a clothes boss.
sentences.zh: 但如果你没有驾驭它的态度和风格，伙计，你只是个衣架子。

sentences.en: Lumberjacks wore plaid.
sentences.zh: 伐木工穿格子衫。

sentences.en: Punks wore plaid miniskirts.
sentences.zh: 朋克穿格子超短裙。

sentences.en: The Beach Boys, I kid you not, used to be called the Pendletones.
sentences.zh: 海滩男孩乐队，我没开玩笑，以前叫“彭德尔顿人”。

sentences.en: And they wore plaid with their surfboards.
sentences.zh: 他们带着冲浪板穿格子衫。

sentences.en: So many different groups have adopted plaid.
sentences.zh: 这么多不同的群体都采用了格子图案。

sentences.en: So it almost doesn't mean anything anymore.
sentences.zh: 所以它几乎不再代表任何意义了。

sentences.en: And really, why are we all wearing this?
sentences.zh: 说真的，我们为什么要穿这个？

sentences.en: This particular pattern, which, once upon a time, was mostly concentrated in the upper corner of this one island off the coast of Europe.
sentences.zh: 这种特殊的图案，曾经主要集中在欧洲海岸外这个岛屿的角落里。

sentences.en: Certainly for Scotland, it's dress.
sentences.zh: 对苏格兰来说，这当然是民族服饰。

sentences.en: Dress is the thing that identifies people in Scotland.
sentences.zh: 服饰是苏格兰人身份的标识。

sentences.en: Dress, people say bagpipes as well.
sentences.zh: 服饰，人们也会提到风笛。

sentences.en: This is Peter MacDonald, historian at the Scottish Tartans Authority.
sentences.zh: 这是彼得·麦克唐纳，苏格兰格子呢管理局的历史学家。

sentences.en: They call this pattern tartan, not plaid.
sentences.zh: 他们把这种图案称为“格子呢”，而不是“格子”。

sentences.en: We don't use that word for patterns in this country.
sentences.zh: 在这个国家，我们不用那个词来形容这种图案。

sentences.en: Plaid is a garment.
sentences.zh: “格子”是一种披肩服饰。

sentences.en: The Scotsmen who lived in the Highlands, the northern hilly part of the country, used to wrap themselves in a cloth.
sentences.zh: 居住在高地（即该国北部多山地区）的苏格兰人过去常把自己裹在布里。

sentences.en: Almost like a blanket.
sentences.zh: 就像毯子一样。

sentences.en: Kind of like an Indian sari.
sentences.zh: 有点像印度的纱丽。

sentences.en: So if you like, it's a tartan sari.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你愿意，它就是一种格子呢纱丽。

sentences.en: We'll be the nearest equivalent.
sentences.zh: 这大概是最接近的对应物了。

sentences.en: That bolt of cloth was called a plaid.
sentences.zh: 那卷布料被称为“格子”。

sentences.en: And it had a tartan pattern on it.
sentences.zh: 上面有格子呢图案。

sentences.en: That's how the term got into the U.S.
sentences.zh: 这就是这个词进入美国的方式。

sentences.en: And that word then becomes synonymous with the pattern.
sentences.zh: 然后这个词就成了这种图案的代名词。

sentences.en: It's not like back then there were tartan shirts and tartan scarves.
sentences.zh: 并不是说当时就有格子呢衬衫和格子呢围巾。

sentences.en: No, tartan was on these traditional plaids and overcoats and on the traditional pants, which were called trues.
sentences.zh: 不，格子呢是出现在这些传统的披肩、外套以及被称为“特鲁斯”的传统裤子上。

sentences.en: Trues are tartan trousers.
sentences.zh: “特鲁斯”就是格子呢长裤。

sentences.en: Well, they're not trousers because they're tights.
sentences.zh: 嗯，它们不是裤子，因为它们是紧身裤。

sentences.en: They included the feet.
sentences.zh: 它们连着脚。

sentences.en: So they're more like ladies' tights, you know.
sentences.zh: 所以它们更像是女士连裤袜，你懂的。

sentences.en: So tartan was kind of this parochial little pattern that Scotsmen in the country used to wear.
sentences.zh: 所以格子呢曾是一种偏远地区的小众图案，是乡下的苏格兰人穿的。

sentences.en: And it was pretty much only used on these obscure traditional Highland garments that I had never heard of before.
sentences.zh: 而且它几乎只用于这些我以前从未听说过的晦涩的传统高地服饰上。

sentences.en: And then something happened.
sentences.zh: 然后发生了一件事。

sentences.en: Something that would end up turning tartan loose on the world.
sentences.zh: 这件事最终让格子呢风靡全球。

sentences.en: These obscure traditional Highland clothes were banned.
sentences.zh: 这些晦涩的传统高地服饰被禁止了。

sentences.en: The act banned kilts, plaids and other elements of Highland dress and outdoor coats in tartan you can't wear as well.
sentences.zh: 该法案禁止了苏格兰短裙、披肩以及其他高地服饰，格子呢外套也不能穿。

sentences.en: The act Peter MacDonald is talking about is the Dress Act of 1746.
sentences.zh: 彼得·麦克唐纳提到的法案是1746年的《服饰法案》。

sentences.en: Scotland was being taken over by the Hanoverian Empire.
sentences.zh: 苏格兰当时正被汉诺威王朝接管。

sentences.en: And many of the Scots who fought back were from the Highlands.
sentences.zh: 许多反抗的苏格兰人来自高地。

sentences.en: And so they wore tartan coats and kilts and plaids.
sentences.zh: 他们穿着格子呢外套、短裙和披肩。

sentences.en: Put in modern parlance, they would be seen as terrorists or freedom fighters depending on which side you were on.
sentences.zh: 用现代的话说，根据你所处的立场，他们会被视为恐怖分子或自由战士。

sentences.en: But that's the reason for the ban.
sentences.zh: 但这就是禁令的原因。

sentences.en: It was a way to suppress the resistance.
sentences.zh: 这是一种镇压抵抗运动的方式。

sentences.en: By limiting what they wore.
sentences.zh: 通过限制他们的穿着。

sentences.en: Men were not allowed to wear Highland clothes for 35 years in Scotland.
sentences.zh: 在苏格兰，男性有35年不被允许穿高地服饰。

sentences.en: But here's the thing.
sentences.zh: 但重点来了。

sentences.en: Just like banned books become the cool thing to read,
sentences.zh: 就像禁书反而成了人们争相阅读的酷物一样，

sentences.en: when Scottish clothes were banned, they became the cool thing to wear.
sentences.zh: 当苏格兰服饰被禁时，它们反而成了人们争相穿戴的酷物。

sentences.en: As always, when you're not allowed to wear something, that means somebody else immediately will.
sentences.zh: 一如既往，当你被禁止穿某样东西时，就意味着别人会立刻去穿它。

sentences.en: This is Jonathan Fair's author of the book Tartan.
sentences.zh: 这是《格子呢》一书的作者乔纳森·费尔。

sentences.en: And he says what the ban did was that it made Highland clothes trendy outside of Scotland.
sentences.zh: 他说，这项禁令反而让高地服饰在苏格兰以外变得时髦起来。

sentences.en: Suddenly, tartan was also being worn in England.
sentences.zh: 突然间，英格兰也开始穿格子呢了。

sentences.en: That moment made tartan a fashionable fabric.
sentences.zh: 那一刻使格子呢成为了一种时尚面料。

sentences.en: It was no longer a sign of indigenous Highlanders.
sentences.zh: 它不再是本土高地人的标志。

sentences.en: It became something that perhaps Lowlanders or English people with Scottish sympathy started to wear.
sentences.zh: 它成了低地人或同情苏格兰的英国人开始穿的东西。

sentences.en: But Scottish men had an option.
sentences.zh: 但苏格兰男人有一个选择。

sentences.en: If they wanted to keep wearing their traditional clothes during the ban, there was a loophole.
sentences.zh: 如果他们想在禁令期间继续穿传统服装，有一个漏洞。

sentences.en: They could go fight for the British Empire.
sentences.zh: 他们可以去为大英帝国打仗。

sentences.en: The ban didn't apply to Scotsmen who joined the army.
sentences.zh: 禁令不适用于加入军队的苏格兰人。

sentences.en: So over time, it encouraged people, if they wanted to continue to wear their native garb, to join the military.
sentences.zh: 所以随着时间的推移，如果人们想继续穿民族服装，这鼓励了他们参军。

sentences.en: This meant Scotsmen wearing tartans were deployed around the world,
sentences.zh: 这意味着穿着格子呢的苏格兰士兵被部署到世界各地，

sentences.en: which influenced the style and popularity of similar-looking patterns across the colonies,
sentences.zh: 这影响了殖民地各地类似图案的风格和流行度，

sentences.en: like madras in India.
sentences.zh: 比如印度的马德拉斯格纹。

sentences.en: Well, I would say madras.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我会说是马德拉斯格纹。

sentences.en: And checkered bandanas in Jamaica.
sentences.zh: 还有牙买加的方格头巾。

sentences.en: And the shuka cloth of the Maasai warriors.
sentences.zh: 以及马赛战士的舒卡布。

sentences.en: The colonialism of the British Empire spread these influences around
sentences.zh: 大英帝国的殖民主义将这些影响传播开来，

sentences.en: and increased global demand for tartan and tartan-like fabrics.
sentences.zh: 并增加了全球对格子呢和类似格子呢面料的需求。

sentences.en: The presence of Highland regimental soldiers wearing tartan in some form or another
sentences.zh: 高地团士兵以某种形式穿着格子呢的出现，

sentences.en: would have influenced people directly on a purely aesthetic way.
sentences.zh: 会直接在纯粹审美层面上影响人们。

sentences.en: And meanwhile, people in England with Scottish sympathies
sentences.zh: 与此同时，英格兰那些同情苏格兰的人，

sentences.en: all got together in 1778 and made a kind of booster group to advocate for Scottish culture.
sentences.zh: 在1778年聚在一起，成立了一个支持团体来倡导苏格兰文化。

sentences.en: Something called the Highland Society of London was formed
sentences.zh: 成立了一个叫“伦敦高地协会”的组织，

sentences.en: in order to try and preserve the customs and manners,
sentences.zh: 旨在试图保护习俗和礼仪，

sentences.en: what was called the Highland Revival, the Great Highland Revival.
sentences.zh: 这就是所谓的“高地复兴”，伟大的高地复兴。

sentences.en: They were responsible for the repeal of the Dress Act in 1782.
sentences.zh: 他们促成了1782年《服饰法案》的废除。

sentences.en: And so by the time the dress ban was finally lifted, it was just like tartan mania.
sentences.zh: 所以当服饰禁令最终解除时，简直是格子呢狂热。

sentences.en: The Great Highland Revival was in full swing.
sentences.zh: 伟大的高地复兴正如火如荼。

sentences.en: Scottish soldiers were coming home and now they could wear their tartan
sentences.zh: 苏格兰士兵回家了，现在他们可以穿上格子呢，

sentences.en: and Englishmen were wearing tartan and people all over the colonies were wearing tartan.
sentences.zh: 英国人在穿，殖民地各地的人们也都在穿格子呢。

sentences.en: And North Americans were really wearing tartan.
sentences.zh: 而北美人民更是真正地穿上了格子呢。

sentences.en: Obviously the kind of work shirt that you would particularly identify with America,
sentences.zh: 显然，那种你特别会与美国联系起来的工作衬衫，

sentences.en: I should say, a kind of plaid working shirt.
sentences.zh: 我应该说，是一种格子工作衬衫。

sentences.en: If you go back, some of the earliest cloths that were used to make those work shirts
sentences.zh: 如果你回溯历史，一些最早用于制作那些工作衬衫的布料，

sentences.en: were exported from Scotland.
sentences.zh: 都是从苏格兰出口的。

sentences.en: Tartan became a massive export to the United States.
sentences.zh: 格子呢成为了出口到美国的大宗商品。

sentences.en: Tartan was a huge export to America in the 1700s, early 1800s.
sentences.zh: 在18世纪和19世纪初，格子呢是出口到美国的大宗商品。

sentences.en: In the United States, tartan was also a symbol of heritage and belonging.
sentences.zh: 在美国，格子呢也是一种传承和归属感的象征。

sentences.en: If you were a Scotsman who was made to flee your homeland.
sentences.zh: 如果你是一个被迫逃离家园的苏格兰人。

sentences.en: Or if you literally belonged to a Scotsman.
sentences.zh: 或者如果你实际上是某个苏格兰人的财产。

sentences.en: There were lots of very powerful Scottish families very active in the slave trade.
sentences.zh: 有很多非常有权势的苏格兰家族积极参与奴隶贸易。

sentences.en: These kinds of records are hard to find.
sentences.zh: 这类记录很难找到。

sentences.en: But it's said that enslaved people across the colonies also wore tartan patterned cloth.
sentences.zh: 但据说殖民地各地的奴隶也穿格子呢图案的布料。

sentences.en: Because tartan is bright and noticeable.
sentences.zh: 因为格子呢鲜艳且引人注目。

sentences.en: Slaves would be made to wear a cloth with a particular tartan,
sentences.zh: 奴隶会被要求穿上带有特定格子呢的布料，

sentences.en: which said who they belonged to.
sentences.zh: 这表明了他们属于谁。

sentences.en: You were being marked, you were being branded by your owners, by your oppressors,
sentences.zh: 你被标记了，被你的主人、你的压迫者打上了烙印，

sentences.en: which is pretty chilling.
sentences.zh: 这真是令人不寒而栗。

sentences.en: But it certainly, for those people, was very much a cloth of oppression.
sentences.zh: 但对那些人来说，这确实在很大程度上是一种压迫的布料。

sentences.en: Tartan has been, in many ways, a cloth of oppression.
sentences.zh: 在许多方面，格子呢一直是一种压迫的布料。

sentences.en: Whether the Scots were being oppressed themselves,
sentences.zh: 无论是苏格兰人自己受到压迫，

sentences.en: or acting as the hand of the British Empire,
sentences.zh: 还是充当大英帝国的帮凶，

sentences.en: or perpetuating the global slave trade.
sentences.zh: 或是延续全球奴隶贸易。

sentences.en: And it functions efficiently as a cloth of oppression
sentences.zh: 它作为一种压迫的布料非常有效，

sentences.en: because it is so loud and highly visible.
sentences.zh: 因为它太张扬且高度显眼。

sentences.en: I do think it has this idea of almost negating the body
sentences.zh: 我确实认为它有一种几乎否定身体的概念，

sentences.en: and becoming literally just the pattern.
sentences.zh: 并真正地变成了图案本身。

sentences.en: So you are literally kind of becoming the brand.
sentences.zh: 所以你实际上是在变成那个品牌。

sentences.en: And tartan can be a brand of so many different conflicting things.
sentences.zh: 而格子呢可以是许多不同冲突事物的品牌。

sentences.en: In the United States, tartan can be a nod to a rugged Highlander.
sentences.zh: 在美国，格子呢可以是对粗犷高地人的致敬。

sentences.en: The idea of the incredibly macho Highlanders who's running around
sentences.zh: 那种极其大男子主义的高地人四处奔跑的形象，

sentences.en: maybe looking after his sheep, only wearing a kilt.
sentences.zh: 也许只穿着短裙在照看他的羊。

sentences.en: Or a monarchic coloniser.
sentences.zh: 或者是一个君主制的殖民者。

sentences.en: Quintessentially American designers such as Ralph Lauren, for example,
sentences.zh: 例如，拉尔夫·劳伦等典型的美国设计师，

sentences.en: frequently use tartan.
sentences.zh: 经常使用格子呢。

sentences.en: I think it is probably associated with ideas of colonialism and empire.
sentences.zh: 我认为它可能与殖民主义和帝国的理念有关。

sentences.en: And that's aside from its associations with queerness,
sentences.zh: 这还不算它与酷儿群体的关联，

sentences.en: or lumberjacks, or cowboys, or bike messengers.
sentences.zh: 或是伐木工、牛仔，又或是自行车快递员的关联。

sentences.en: Quite literally, there's a tartan for everything.
sentences.zh: 毫不夸张地说，万物皆可有格纹。

sentences.en: These are the tartan swatches.
sentences.zh: 这些就是格纹样本。

sentences.en: Dee Williams works at the National Records of Scotland.
sentences.zh: 迪·威廉姆斯在苏格兰国家档案馆工作。

sentences.en: In these boxes here.
sentences.zh: 就在这些盒子里。

sentences.en: And she is showing me the Scottish Register of Tartans,
sentences.zh: 她正在向我展示《苏格兰格纹登记册》，

sentences.en: which is very much not open to the public.
sentences.zh: 这地方通常是不对外开放的。

sentences.en: How often does someone come to...
sentences.zh: 平时会有多少人来……

sentences.en: They don't.
sentences.zh: 没人会来。

sentences.en: That's the point.
sentences.zh: 重点就在这儿。

sentences.en: You are the firSt.
sentences.zh: 你是第一个。

sentences.en: Well...
sentences.zh: 好吧……

sentences.en: She said I was the first journalist who had been in there.
sentences.zh: 她说我是第一个获准进入那里的记者。

sentences.en: Genuinely, we don't offer this.
sentences.zh: 说实话，我们通常不提供这种参观。

sentences.en: We don't say to people, come in and look at all the swatches.
